nodes.description: In OTULIN-deficient fibroblasts LUBAC is degraded and its recruitment to the TNF receptor signaling complex falls, so the fibroblast TNF-mediated signaling response is reduced rather than increased. This cell-type-specific LUBAC degradation is the defining result of Damgaard et al. 2019 and is the mirror image of the increased NF-kappaB seen in monocytes.

nodes.description: Allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation produced complete resolution of inflammation in a transplanted patient, demonstrating that haematopoietic cells drive the clinical disease. The disease relapsed nine months later as donor chimerism fell, so HSCT is potentially curative rather than an established cure.

nodes.description: Because ORAS is driven by dysregulated TNF signaling and TNF-induced cell death, TNF inhibition is mechanistically rational and ameliorates inflammation in patients. Agents used include the monoclonal antibodies infliximab and adalimumab and the receptor-fusion protein etanercept; because the class spans both antibody and fusion-protein platforms, no single therapeutic_modality value is asserted.

evidence.reference_title: OTULIN deficiency in ORAS causes cell type-specific LUBAC degradation, dysregulated TNF signalling and cell death.
evidence.snippet: Treatment with TNF inhibitors such as antibodies (e.g. infliximab) or TNF blockers (e.g. etanercept) effectively ameliorates inflammation, but there is currently no cure for ORAS.
